rows: Let me say this plainly. Nobody in this room needs to be frightened tonight. Everybody needs to be ready.
Brawling is fine when the people around you can walk home afterwards. That is my test.
A risk falls on whoever is least able to refuse it. Let us keep that in mind.
Pace is a decision I share with the people I am responsible for. Tonight, I share it with you.
The people deserve a match that is looked after from the first bell to the last. That is my job.
The opportunity is real, and I am here to protect it.
I have worked for every bit of this, and I want the young people around me to have the same chance.
Look at the stance; it is sound. It is calm, and it is the way I want the young ones to stand.
You bring up technique, and it matters. Show me a hold you could teach to someone who has never done it.
Strikes are part of the lesson. Land them clean, and nobody gets hurt for the sake of it.
A risk I take is one I can explain to everyone who relies on me. Can you do the same?
A stall is a waste of the opportunity. I would rather you did not waste it.
The people want a match they can trust. Give them one, and I will do the same.
You call me a passenger. I am the one who takes responsibility when it matters.
You are proud of your {strength}. Keep it steady for the young ones. That is fine. Be proud of it without putting anybody at risk.
I have been thinking about your {strength}, and I want to find a way to meet it that keeps everybody safe.
You held firm. Good. Sensible. Calm is how you look after the people in the next match.
Your point is taken. We agree on that, and that is a good place to start.
I could give you a hard time about that. I would rather give you a fair one.
One pin, and the team is safe. Keep me down, and I will say you did it fairly.
On the mat I will look after you, and I will expect you to look after me.
Grounded or standing, the job is the same: nobody gets hurt for the sake of a moment.
Stand where I can see you. I want to see your best, and I want to see you safe.
A better answer, thank you. I can build on that.
You have sidestepped the question. Take your time, and then give me something solid.
Your point is taken. I will take that on board.
I will let that stand. We will settle it at the bell.
I will wrestle this match with care, and I will make sure we both leave in good order.
My approach is steady and fair. You will see it on the night, in the right way.
Whatever happens, I want everybody who looked up to me to be proud of how I acted.
The responsibility is still open. There is still a responsibility on the table.
I have one more thing to say, and you will hear it when the bell rings.
I'm supposed to keep people safe, including from a charge I can't establish. I shouldn't have made that one.
I can ask you to take care in the ring. I cannot claim you did something without a proper example.
Then leave the accusation there. We'll keep our minds on looking after each other when we wrestle.
That's fair. We don't need an unsupported charge to make this a serious contest.
They'll see if we can work hard without losing sight of our responsibilities to each other.
The referee and the crowd can judge what happens in the match. We don't need to put anyone's character on trial.
Let us give these people something they can judge for themselves. What can we demonstrate together in the ring?
What can we show the young ones about doing this properly, without relying on an allegation?
You've thought about my {strength}, which is good preparation. Now show me you can answer them without losing control of the contest.
I will use my {strength} responsibly. You still have to do your own work to meet them.
That's fair. It would be irresponsible of me to pass on something I cannot verify.
I take that on board. We should be accountable for what we know, not what we suspect.
Your experience deserves respect. It does not make the person across from you any less entitled to a fair contest.
Years of work ought to teach us how to face a new opponent, not give us a reason to dismiss them.
Experience helps me recognise the moment a contest stops being useful to either wrestler.
I've learned to adjust the work when the original plan puts somebody in an unnecessary predicament.
